transcript: this is my MCU, folks! after the acclaimed film versions of Fences and Ma Rainy's Black Bottom we now have the third film in this series based on August Wilson's Century Cycle and this one is coming on the heels of a recent Broadway revival which I actually saw and it starred several of the same cast members including John David Washington and Samuel L Jackson I liked that Broadway revival but I will say one difference that I noticed right off the bat is that this film is definitely a lot more streamlined the film is like 45 minutes shorter and I'm not sure how much of that was cuts to the script vs. just kinda picking up the pace seems like maybe it was a little bit of both on some level I definitely appreciate this because I think the Broadway revival did drag a little bit in its pacing at some points although I will also say that I think they might have overcorrected a little bit for this film cause I think we've lost some of that sense of really getting to sit with these characters and sit in the world of the play so I don't know maybe ideally they could have found somewhere in the middle there is definitely a lot to like about this film in particular I actually think some of the performances worked better than they did on Broadway when I saw John David Washington in this role on Broadway he had that same big firecracker energy but it was a little bit one note meanwhile in this version I think he was a little better at finding those levels like the peaks and valleys in the energy also worth noting that Danielle Deadwyler is playing the role that Danielle Brooks played on stage and to be clear I am a big fan of Danielle Brooks I think she is a phenomenally skilled actor but I think this role in particular is a little bit better suited to the strength of Danielle Deadwyler as far as the text itself it's not necessarily my favorite August Wilson play but it is still extraordinary the way that he uses this piano to anchor the plot, the themes, and the character arcs all at the same time perfectly in sync and interwoven with each other in a beautiful, emotionally nuanced way to really feel the weight of what it means to both Boy Willie and Berniece so that when they are in conflict with each other it feels completely earned and believable on both sides just a great reminder of why August Wilson is the GOAT as far as how well they translated it to the screen like I know this conversation always comes up every time they adapt into a film of like did they do enough to “open it up” and make it feel like a film and not just a play on screen in this case I would say yes and no maybe leaning a little bit more toward no but I also have issues with that line of logic in the first place I do genuinely understand that drama like this doesn't always play as well on screen and you do always want something to feel like it fits the medium that it's in but I also feel like it's not the biggest crime for it to still feel like a play especially when you consider that the context of this project is to preserve these plays in a visual medium and you might say why didn't Netflix just film it on Broadway instead of making this movie? but I appreciate having the movie because I think it gives them the opportunity to kind of recalibrate the performances so that they play better on camera in a way that is a lot more difficult to do with a pro-shot not to mention there are moments when the director Malcolm Washington finds ways to make it feel more cinematic and those moments are really quite beautiful
